rubric_notes: Complete. Verified a.22.1 families, sunids, and example domains (7ybf, d1f1ea_, 2byk/2bym, d1r4va_). States superfamily implies probable common ancestor despite low sequence similarity, rejects transfer of tails/modifications/octamer/DNA wrapping outside a.22.1.1, and notes class/fold sharing is not homology. Linker histone a.4.5.13 lineage is correct though not in this bundle; phrased as 'no evidence' of homology. CENP-A/H2A.Z placement stated generally, not fabricated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Lineages with all sunids and boundaries supported by bundle (release 2.08 in node records). Superfamily correctly framed as stronger than fold but weaker than family; probable remote homology. Rejects both directions of function transfer, notes hypothetical-protein status, Li/UNL non-evidence, alignment needed for active-site equivalence, boundary difference, and release specificity. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Correct families with sunids, superfamily c.55.1, fold c.55, class c and the duplication comment, all supported by the bundle. Infers ancient shared origin and a common cleft phosphoryl/nucleotide-binding and lobe-closure mechanism, explicitly as generalisations not specific functions; refuses to transfer function, substrate, catalytic residues, regulation, cellular role, oligomeric state; notes hexokinase vs glucokinase are separate families. Fold-level neighbours not claimed homologous. Description of other c.55 groups as 'nucleotidyltransferase/nuclease' is loose but immaterial. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Hierarchy, sunids, comments, members supported. Correct remote-homology interpretation with conserved bimetal site as evidence beyond fold; clearly rejects function/metal/assembly transfer; lists external evidence. Phrase 'possibly analogous' for other a.25 superfamilies is hedged, not an assertion of convergence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Correct families, sunids, lineage and curator comments supported by bundle. Explains superfamily as probable distant homology stronger than fold (which can be convergent) but weaker than family; rejects transfer of copper binding/redox function citing family comments; lists ligand-position alignment checks plus direct experimental metal/redox evidence; rejects reverse transfer and cross-family template use for active sites. No material omissions.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. All classifications and sibling superfamilies match the bundle. Superfamily correctly read as probable distant homology; fold sharing alone not homology; family split means no shared function. Rejects transferring conjugation, p97 binding and Ras binding by name, plus binding-site residue mapping; template and representative limits and required external evidence stated. Unsupported adjective 'large' for d.15.1.0 is immaterial.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Correct families, sunids, superfamily, sibling families, Pfam PF03709 and KaiA annotation, all supported by bundle. Superfamily-level probable common ancestry clearly distinguished from fold sharing and from family-level closeness. Rejects phosphorylation/two-component signaling for KaiA-N and ODC wing, decarboxylase/PLP transfer, partner/pathway transfer, and template misuse; notes wing is a structural sub-domain of a multidomain enzyme and KaiA clock activity lies in the C-terminal domain. Limits and needed evidence stated.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Hierarchy, sunids, homology_scope=sf, PubMed citation all bundle-supported; reasoning fully meets must_include (fold = geometric statement, no cross-superfamily ancestry asserted or denied, V1/A1 homologous within one family), limits stated, background knowledge flagged. Factual imprecision: describes the bulge as an insertion 'in the N-terminal beta-barrel region'; SCOPe boundaries show it inserted within the discontinuous c.37.1.11 P-loop domain (b.49.1.2 is continuous 1-70). Noncentral.

Fold, sunids, superfamilies, and fold comment all supported by bundle. Correct fold-vs-superfamily reasoning, convergence raised as possibility with distant homology explicitly not ruled out, rejects function/template transfer, and lists sequence-profile, motif, structural (FATCAT/DALI), and independent-classification evidence needed. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct families, superfamily c.2.1, fold, sunids, family comment and PF02254, all supported. Superfamily carries the curated common-ancestry claim (remote homologs); fold describes geometry only; separate families mean divergent function, ligand and context. Explicitly bars dehydrogenase, CoA-ligase or gating function and cofactor specificity transfer; requires family-specific support (partner domains, zinc ligands, channel context) and external evidence; notes Rossmann-like structural matches outside c.2.1 are not homology evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct lineage, sunids, ligand comments; correct conclusion that the generic family-rank homology flag does not override class-k semantics, with good transfer limits. Checked class-node annotations (empty, supported) but never the family node, so the decisive 'not a true family' annotation on 100905 is absent.

All must_include met: 1.69 c.137/c.137.1/c.137.1.1 own lineage vs c.23.14.1; 2.08 d1t1ja1/d1t1jb1 (1-118) c.23.14.2 vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 sharing c.23.14; superfamily rename; family sunid 110461 preserved; tag domains l.1.1.1. States placement already in 1.73 (bundle-supported) without asserting it was first. Evolutionary interpretation correct: recognised as flavodoxin-like variant probably sharing ancestry, superfamily = probable common ancestry not close homology; function not transferable; SID mapping via sunids. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

All criteria met with bundle-supported lineages, annotations and sequences. Notes QVQLQQSG matches VH FR1 and is plausibly primer-encoded, clearly labeled as inference, while retaining the SCOPe artifact classification. Rejects tag similarity as homology evidence, notes 8-residue matches lack statistical power, and requires superfamily-level support rather than fold alone for an Ig relationship. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1; 2026-10-14.

Accurate and complete: d1acca_ (43828, f.11.1.1) as a whole-chain domain in 1.75 and 2.01-2.03 with every level a singleton, split from 2.04 and confirmed through 2.08 into d1acca2 (238522, A:14-225, b.179.1.1) and d1acca1 (238521, A:226-735, f.60.1.1), with f.11 retired and sid remapping required. Reads the former family as a fusion of independently inherited units, uses GLEYA and GH31 PA14-like families as evidence of module mobility, and states that separate class and fold placement means SCOPe asserts no homology rather than proving none. Blocks toxin and receptor-binding transfer from a PA14 hit in both directions and notes that old-label false positives may be genuine homologs.

Correct five-domain decomposition with sccs, boundaries and sunids matching the bundle; d3jb9a5 47-697 d.394 new fold; a4 bromodomain family, a3 e.8.1.8, a2 c.52.1.36, a1 c.55.3.14. Explicitly separates superfamily-level homology from fold-level similarity, rejects catalytic/acetyl-lysine transfer, notes Jab1/MPN not covered, species-specific numbering, cryo-EM resolution caveat, maturase origin flagged as published interpretation. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14.

Complete: identifies the family as a repeat family defined by the repeating unit, gives full lineage with sunids and TaxIds, lengths 51/373/752, the 'single repeat' comment, the 're' caveat quoted as the curatorial statement that the common domain is a variable-copy-number array, and the canonical repeat unit 4cj9 A:259-292 with correct coordinate_scope and per-node applicability. Distinguishes family-level curated ancestry from fold-level architecture, notes BurrH as a sequence-divergent outlier placed on architecture plus curation rather than pairwise identity, blocks RVD/target and template transfer, and uses the empty xref sections to state that Pfam and literature evidence must come from outside SCOPe. Evaluator: Claude SCOPe benchmark grader, 2026-10-14.

Reports 2.08 / 2.08-stable with freeze and release dates and periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16 (matches evidence bundle; suite gold lists 2.08-2023-01-06 but bundle-supported value not penalized). Recommends citing stable 2.08 pinned in API calls, recording the dated periodic label and access date, and explicitly warns against relying on 'current'. Describes periodic label as automated update layered on 2.08 adding newly classified PDB entries, not a new numbered or curated release. 'Adds or refreshes content' is slightly vague but not wrong. All must_include and must_avoid criteria met.

Meets all must_include items: same a.47.2.1 lineage for 1br0/1ez3/1dn1 B; fragment comment and 'ms' flag retrieved; a.47 four-long-helix definition cited to show the three-helix fragments resemble a spectrin repeat and would be mis-assigned on their own, with the fold inferred from the complete domain (1dn1/3c98); d1dn1b_ as automated match to curated d3c98b_ on an obsolete entry. Correctly keeps spectrin resemblance as non-homology without asserting analogy, places homology at superfamily/family, rejects function transfer from a.47, recommends full-domain template with closed-conformation caveat, and lists external evidence. No release-history comparison, but not required by the prompt. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Clear convergence/divergence split with correct level semantics (superfamily deepest homology claim; fold not evidence), domain-by-domain treatment of GAPDH/ADH, and a closing caveat that cross-fold similarity may be undetectable deep ancestry so the conclusion is 'homology not demonstrated', not 'proven unrelated'. Evidence integration covers profile/HMM, whole-domain topology, cofactor binding mode, shared insertions, SCOP assignment. All lineages (c.2.1, c.3.1, c.4.1, c.1.7 in TIM barrel, c.77.1, c.25.1, d.81.1 class d, b.35.1) supported by bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correctly reports 2.04 as class-level-only sharing with ColG in its own superfamily b.23.2 under CUB-like b.23 versus Cry3A in b.18.1 under b.18, then the 2.05-onward placement in new family b.18.1.36 (sunid 267607) inside b.18.1 with b.18.1.3 unchanged and families still distinct. Chain B domain and the l.1.1.1 two-residue tag are handled correctly. Uses the retrieved family comment to assemble the three-way structure-based link and correctly identifies d1w99a3 as a Cry domain-III entry in the same family as Cry3A and d2quoa_ as its own family b.18.1.37. Explicitly states that a shared sandwich fold alone would not establish ancestry, that the placement is a curated inference rather than proof, that family-level traits including ligand specificity and Ca sites must not be transferred, that the other Cry3A domains are unrelated, and that the cited paper was not read. Evaluator: Claude, 2026-10-14.

Correct lineage, sunids, boundaries, comments, hf definition and homology flags; quality values match retrieved records and the 4 A effective resolution is correctly identified as a fallback. Homology framed as same-sequence variants; hf as sequence-based retention without structural match; rejects template swap, structural label use and function transfer; covers leakage, stratification and representative selection; separates quality from correctness; background mechanism flagged as not from SCOPe.

All must_include met: family-level homology explicitly contrasted with superfamily/fold strength; fr flag tied to 99 vs 50 residue coverage with missing segments named; alignment limited to observed strands, unresolved positions as missing data not gaps; representative must be complete domain, entry-level SPACI (1o5d 0.287 vs 1uc6 0.022) cannot override; fragment retained only if labelled partial-coverage, excluded from variability stats. No function transfer. Identifiers, annotations and quality values match bundle; admits ASTRAL subsets not checked. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. All must_include met: new superfamily in existing fold; family asserts homology and closer relationship (~30% identity or strong structure+function); new fold only if core topology differs, peripheral decorations insufficient; assignment is a revisable hypothesis with listed evidence types; structural scores alone insufficient. Convergence stated as possibility, not fact. d.58 example (sunid 54861, d.58.1-d.58.5) supported by bundle. No material errors.

Correct superfamily and family identifiers with sunids supported by the bundle. Superfamily read as probable homology beyond fold, with shared core motifs and mechanism; substrate, regulation, inhibitor sensitivity and activity explicitly not transferable, with a useful caveat on automated-match family d.144.1.0. Evidence list includes close homology, active-site check, substrate-site match, regulatory elements in full-length architecture, and experimental data.
